cases.sentence: Поговорив еще несколько времени с эсаулом о ___, которое теперь, глядя на близость французов, Денисов, казалось, окончательно решил, он повернул лошадь и поехал назад.
cases.explain: «завтрашнем нападении» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: After talking for some time with the esaul about next day’s attack, which now, seeing how near they were to the French, he seemed to have definitely decided on, Denísov turned his horse and rode back.

cases.sentence: Подъезжая к ___, Денисов остановился, вглядываясь в лес.
cases.explain: «лесной караулке» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: As they approached the watchhouse Denísov stopped, peering into the forest. Among the trees a man with long legs and long, swinging arms, wearing a short jacket, bast shoes, and a Kazán hat, was approaching with long, light steps. He had a musketoon over his shoulder and an ax stuck in his girdle. When he espied Denísov he hastily threw something into the bushes, removed his sodden hat by its floppy brim, and approached his commander. It was Tíkhon. His wrinkled and pockmarked face and narrow little eyes beamed with self-satisfied merriment. He lifted his head high and gazed at Denísov as if repressing a laugh.

cases.sentence: По лесу, между деревьев большими легкими шагами шел на ___, с длинными мотающимися руками человек в куртке, лаптях и казанской шляпе с ружьем через плечо и топором за поясом.
cases.explain: «длинных ногах» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.

cases.sentence: Изрытое оспой и морщинами лицо его с маленькими ___ сияло самодовольным весельем.
cases.explain: «узкими глазами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

cases.sentence: — То-то мы с горы видели как ты стречка задавал, через лужи-то, — сказал эсаул суживая свои ___.
cases.explain: «блестящие глаза» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Yes, we saw from the hill how you took to your heels through the puddles!” said the esaul, screwing up his glittering eyes.

cases.sentence: Как же, говорит, я сам ___, не пойду, говорит.
cases.explain: «анаральский сын» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, but he was a regular good-for-nothing,” said Tíkhon. “The clothes on him—poor stuff! How could I bring him? And so rude, your honor! Why, he says: ‘I’m a general’s son myself, I won’t go!’ he says.”

cases.sentence: И до ___ он ехал сердито нахмурившись и молча.
cases.explain: «самой караулки» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Well, let’s go,” said Denísov, and rode all the way to the watchhouse in silence and frowning angrily.

cases.sentence: Он оглянулся на ___ и что-то кольнуло его в сердце.
cases.explain: «пленного барабанщика» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: When the fit of laughter that had seized him at Tíkhon’s words and smile had passed and Pétya realized for a moment that this Tíkhon had killed a man, he felt uneasy. He looked round at the captive drummer boy and felt a pang in his heart. But this uneasiness lasted only a moment. He felt it necessary to hold his head higher, to brace himself, and to question the esaul with an air of importance about tomorrow’s undertaking, that he might not be unworthy of the company in which he found himself.

cases.sentence: Он почувствовал необходимость повыше поднять голову, подбодриться и расспросить эсаула с ___ о завтрашнем предприятии с тем, чтобы не быть недостойным того общества, в котором он находился.
cases.explain: «значительным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
